To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the superconductivity in disordered films can be explained by a theory of electron pairing near the Anderson mobility edge; (b) this theory is based on a novel concept of the "fractal superconductivity" which is a consequence of the fact that, in the presence of the Anderson mobility edge, the electron pairing is not suppressed by the disorder but, on the contrary, is strongly enhanced; (c) the "fractal pairing" leads to the superconducting transition temperature

(1) the superconductivity in poor conductors is due to electron pairing in the localized states, (2) the pairing is mediated by virtual transitions into the extended states, (3) the critical temperature $T_c$ is a function of the Fermi energy $T_c(E_F)$ with a pronounced minimum near $E_c$ (the Anderson mobility edge) and (4) the minimum is due to the interplay between the pairing and localization mechanisms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of electron localization in the presence of strong electron-electron interaction and disorder in the system.

a search of a new mechanism of superconductivity, which is based on an idea that superconductivity is possible in the systems in which Fermi level is located in the energy gap between localized and extended states.
the physics of electron pairing in disordered systems, and with the resulting superconductivity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the theory of superconductivity in poor metals is not well established yet.
the theory of superconductivity near the mobility edge is not yet developed.
the pairing mechanism is not the conventional BCS mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the superconductivity near the localization threshold is a phenomenon that is not only possible, but is also a very natural consequence of the electron pairing mechanism.

the superconductivity in poor conductors near the localization threshold is a phenomenon of the same nature as the superconductivity of conventional type, with the only difference being that it is not due to the conventional electron pairing mechanism, but rather to the electron pairing due to the Coulomb interaction.

we have developed a theory of superconductivity in disordered metals in which Fermi level is located in the vicinity of mobility edge $E_{c}$ and the superconducting transition temperature $T_c$ is of order $1$K.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the superconducting transition temperature $T_c$ is not a monotonic function of $E_F$ and can even have a maximum at a distance from the mobility edge, where $E_c$ and $E_F$ differ by a few times the Thouless energy.

the critical temperature $T_c$ is determined by a competition of two effects: (i) an increase in the effective electron-electron interaction due to localization of electrons and (ii) the decrease in electron density of states due to Anderson localization.
in the vicinity of the mobility edge $E_F\approx E_c$ the system becomes a superconductor with a very small critical temperature $T_c\sim E_c-E_F$.
